narr: A weak shortwave trough moving across the state aided in the development of showers and thunderstorms across south-central Arizona on the morning of the 14th. With anomalously high amounts of moisture in place, showers and thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall which led to some flash flooding. Flash flooding was reported in northern Pinal County near Florence where Maricopa County Flood Control gages recorded over 1.50 of rainfall. Flash flooding was also reported in the Globe area as heavy rainfall over the recent Telegraph burn scar led to enhanced runoff in Pinal Creek. No injuries or damage were reported.
ev: Images from local broadcast media show a portion of 48th Street in Ahwatukee blocked off due to flooding.

Heavy rainfall over the Florence area led to flash flooding. According to the Pinal County Sheriff's dispatch, Cooper road between Arizona Farms Road and Judd Road was closed to due running washes. No injuries or damage was reported.

Heavy rainfall over the recent Telegraph burn scar led to enhanced runoff into Pinal Creek, which resulted in flash flooding. At 0830MST, a trained weather spotter reported swiftly moving water estimated to be several feet deep flowing over Beer Tree Crossing Road at Pinal Creek in the Globe area. No injuries or damage was reported.
